requirement: Deliver OpenATDD 1.0 as a simple requirement-to-verified-delivery framework with adaptive task depth, recommended human decisions, concise acceptance and solution confirmation, conditional subagents, a local semantic knowledge graph, scoped context, deterministic verification, and real-agent evaluation.

items.title: A developer completes the normal two-confirmation journey without process ceremony
items.given: An initialized supported repository and a one-line feature requirement.
items.when: The developer starts OpenATDD and responds to any material product, scope, cost, risk, or authorization decisions.
items.then: OpenATDD asks no discoverable or routine process questions, every human decision includes a grounded recommendation and 2-3 choices, the developer confirms only the concise completion standards and solution before implementation, and receives a prepared UAT handoff without additional routine approvals.
items.evidence: Quick, Standard, and Deep agent-scenario transcripts, persisted decision records, the approved cards, and the generated UAT report.

items.title: Task depth controls investigation and subagents without changing the user contract
items.given: Representative low-risk local, cross-module, and high-risk or novel task scenarios.
items.when: OpenATDD classifies each task and prepares its investigation plan.
items.then: It records Quick, Standard, or Deep with reasons; applies deterministic risk escalators; keeps Quick local and direct; and uses external research, clean-context execution, or independent review subagents only when the selected depth calls for them.
items.evidence: Routing fixtures, hard-risk regression tests, structured routing output, and recorded agent-dispatch traces.

items.title: The approved solution is concise, project-fitting, and progressively disclosed from one source
items.given: Approved completion standards with every blocking human decision resolved.
items.when: OpenATDD drafts and reviews the solution before presenting it.
items.then: One `solution.md` provides a one-screen recommendation, rationale, changes, material risks, and exclusions followed by optional concise details; every acceptance ID is traced; no material choice is hidden only in the details; unnecessary architecture is rejected; and any post-approval edit invalidates the solution approval.
items.evidence: The rendered solution document, simplicity and consistency review output, contract-validation regressions, and human readability judgment.

items.title: A rebuildable semantic graph retrieves relevant knowledge and expands impact analysis
items.given: Tasks, decisions, acceptance criteria, solutions, paths, incidents, invariants, standards, research, checks, and evidence with source artifacts.
items.when: Those artifacts are approved, resolved, finalized, queried, changed, missing from the index, or rebuilt.
items.then: OpenATDD maintains a local source-hashed node-and-edge index with provenance, marks stale entries, rebuilds missing runtime indexes, returns only relevant relationships, and combines semantic relationships with the existing conservative path fallback to identify historical acceptance that needs reverification.
items.evidence: Graph build/query/impact fixtures, stale and missing-index regressions, provenance assertions, and affected-history integration tests.

items.title: Implementation, verification, recovery, and learning receive scoped context
items.given: An approved task with routing, decision, graph, memory, and environment facts.
items.when: OpenATDD prepares implementation, verification, a fresh-context subagent, or a resumed repair attempt.
items.then: It supplies only relevant source-hashed context, keeps implementation and verification views distinct, persists a compact recovery boundary, records repair hypotheses and progress, promotes resolved defects into incidents and invariants, and does not mandate TDD, worktrees, a particular architecture, or multi-agent execution.
items.evidence: Context-selection fixtures, resume and bounded-repair regressions, subagent context traces, and incident/invariant graph assertions.

items.title: Existing projects migrate without weakening deterministic delivery
items.given: Existing schema v1/v2 tasks and v0.3 project artifacts, including projects with absent rebuildable indexes.
items.when: They are loaded, upgraded, approved, validated, repaired, and finalized under 1.0.
items.then: Existing contracts, evidence, history, environment observations, and readiness semantics remain valid; missing indexes are recreated; product code remains blocked before both approvals; fresh evidence, verification epochs, complete reruns, source freeze, atomic finalization, credential safety, and affected-history reverification continue to be enforced.
items.evidence: State-migration and legacy-project fixtures, complete deterministic tests, dry-run/finalization evidence, and compatibility validation.

items.title: Real-agent evaluation detects interaction and delivery regressions
items.given: Decision, routing, simplicity, recovery, graph, seed-repository, and hidden-acceptance scenarios plus a configured agent adapter.
items.when: The 1.0 evaluation command runs against the current Skill and a bare-agent baseline where applicable.
items.then: It reports deterministic and real-agent outcomes, human turns, unnecessary questions, research misroutes, missed human decisions, over-engineering, contract violations, first-pass acceptance, token/time cost, and repeatability without treating model claims as test evidence.
items.evidence: Versioned fixtures and rubrics, runner output, hidden-test results, baseline comparison, and a human review of assisted judgments.

items.title: OpenATDD 1.0 remains portable, documented, and independently usable
items.given: A clean Node.js 20+ project with no OpenSpec or other workflow framework installed.
items.when: A developer installs or copies the package, initializes a project, invokes help and the Skill, runs the documented checks, and packs the release.
items.then: Version 1.0 provides the complete natural-language-to-UAT workflow, CLI semantics are covered by real-process regressions, the Skill validates on supported hosts, existing granular commands remain available for debugging, and the distributable contains all required runtime and documentation files.
items.evidence: Install/copy smoke tests, CLI process tests, Skill validation, package dry-run contents, documentation checks, and `npm run check` output.

issues.symptom: Chinese conversations still receive English template and UAT report labels even though no language option should be required.
issues.rootCause: Human-facing templates, contract aliases, and report rendering were hard-coded to English instead of deriving display language from the current requirement and solution artifacts.
regression: human-facing templates and reports infer Chinese without a language option
issues.invariant: Human-facing artifacts follow the conversation language carried by requirement and solution content without a language flag, configuration, or selection prompt.

issues.symptom: Formal finalization marks ASSISTED criteria passed before the required human judgment and evidence boundary is complete.
issues.rootCause: Finalization collapsed prepared evidence and required human judgment into one passed status for every criterion classification.
regression: formal finalization keeps ASSISTED and MANUAL criteria manual and rejects ASSISTED self-pass
issues.invariant: Only AUTO acceptance can be finalized as passed; ASSISTED and MANUAL always remain explicit human judgments.

issues.symptom: The solution summary order and review gate do not deterministically enforce risks, exclusions, consistency, or independent reviewer evidence.
issues.rootCause: The solution contract checked named sections but not their progressive order, and a free-form review lacked complete checks and independent reviewer provenance.
regression: and independent scoped-review dispatch are enforced
issues.invariant: A solution can pass review only when its complete human summary precedes details and every required review check is bound to the current hash and reviewer evidence.

issues.symptom: Resumed repairs and dispatched fresh-context agents are not automatically supplied the scoped implementation or verification context.
issues.rootCause: Resume, repair, and Agent dispatch recorded control state but did not invoke one shared scoped-context loader for the appropriate surface.
regression: and Agent dispatch restore and record source-hashed scoped context
issues.invariant: Every resumed delivery action and fresh-context Agent receives the current source-hashed implementation or verification view before work continues.

issues.symptom: The semantic graph does not ingest project standards or research and does not derive shared-invariant task impacts automatically.
issues.rootCause: Graph discovery omitted standards and research directories, while invariants were keyed by incident identity instead of canonical content.
regression: standards and research enter scoped graph context and shared invariant content derives task impacts without path overlap
issues.invariant: Relevant standards, research, and canonical invariant relationships remain source-hashed, rebuildable inputs to context and impact analysis.

issues.symptom: The release finalization claims Agent evaluation coverage without a persisted report from an actual model and bare-agent comparison.
issues.rootCause: Formal acceptance relied on mock evaluation tests because no bundled real-model adapter, persisted-report verifier, or pass-rate guard existed.
regression: bundled Codex primary and bare adapters run twice and finalization verifies a 100-percent primary real-model report
issues.invariant: A formal real-Agent claim requires repeated hidden-check evidence from the bundled real-model adapter; mock or partial-pass reports never satisfy it.

details.requirement: Deliver OpenATDD 1.0 as a simple requirement-to-verified-delivery framework with adaptive task depth, recommended human decisions, concise acceptance and solution confirmation, conditional subagents, a local semantic knowledge graph, scoped context, deterministic verification, and real-agent evaluation.

attempts.hypothesis: English-only parser and report labels ignored the conversation language carried by requirement and solution artifacts.
attempts.summary: Localized aliases, auto inference, and Chinese report rendering pass focused regressions.

attempts.hypothesis: ASSISTED status was derived from finalization evidence instead of preserving the criterion's required human judgment boundary.
attempts.summary: ASSISTED and MANUAL criteria now remain manual while AUTO alone can pass; focused and full regressions pass.

attempts.hypothesis: The progressive solution parser validated section presence but not summary-first ordering or structured review completeness and reviewer provenance.
attempts.summary: Summary-first ordering, six review checks, and independent Agent context provenance are enforced and covered.

attempts.hypothesis: Resume, repair, and Agent dispatch stored workflow state without automatically resolving the relevant scoped-context view.
attempts.summary: Resume, repair, and dispatch now load and record source-hashed implementation or verification context.

attempts.hypothesis: Graph sources were limited to task and incident artifacts, and task impact relied on explicit IDs or overlapping paths instead of canonical invariant content.
attempts.summary: Standards and research are ingested, invariants are canonicalized, and shared-invariant task impacts are derived.

attempts.hypothesis: The evaluation runner supported external commands but formal finalization only executed deterministic mock tests and accepted a real-model flag without a passing-result condition.
attempts.summary: A bundled Codex adapter produced a repeated real/bare report, real pass claims require 100%, and finalization verifies the persisted report.

repair.lastHypothesis: The evaluation runner supported external commands but formal finalization only executed deterministic mock tests and accepted a real-model flag without a passing-result condition.
